25.explanation: The earlier white control retained authored shadows. With an unshadowed unit camera-headlight, native CPU shows the same major arms and dense sphere grid as unchanged FPT.

38.explanation: Removing authored shadows and matching the key direction reveals dense native geometry and the same narrow horizon gap. No camera, formula or threshold change was needed.

48.explanation: Both original GPU backends fail to preserve the CPU reference at a zoom smaller than world-coordinate float32 spacing. Subsequent field/ray and three-term experiments below establish coordinate/parameter sensitivity and recover the tested geometry in an isolated offline prototype. The production release path remains unchanged; native OpenCL also imposes a different threshold floor.
48.camera_basis_caveat: FPT subtracts camera/target in float64 before casting the direction; the observation does not prove a zero/incorrect camera basis.

experiments: Serial 160-maximum-axis 1-SPP FPT reproductions and native CPU/OpenCL white controls for all three outliers.
Native white controls with shadows disabled for 25/38 exposed the comparison confound.
Warning-free 300-maximum-axis native CPU headlight controls for 25/38, compared with the original 32-SPP FPT captures.
Inspected generated formulas, hybrid finalizers, thresholds and camera conversion. No evaluator/camera experiment was retained or claimed as a fix.

precision_followup.finding: Camera-coordinate rounding and authored formula-parameter rounding independently alter the CPU geometry. GPU absolute-position readback proves first-step stalls and large ray-direction errors. This establishes concrete precision failures, not just a cross-backend correlation.
caveats: Readback uses a separate diagnostic kernel calling production evaluator/march helpers; no production shader was changed.

GPU displacement is calculated on the host from rounded absolute positions. The initial in-shader subtract-origin diagnostic was invalidated because fast math cancelled the rounding; it is not used for these results.
The CPU parameter experiment rounds five explicit settings in each of two formula sections, not all derived constants or arithmetic.
RGB metrics quantify control-image differences, not exact geometric error. CPU columns share lighting; the FPT image uses a different neutral key.
This initial precision follow-up did not include a high-precision implementation. The separate prototype below now passes an isolated numerical gate, not release-renderer parity.

high_low_precision_prototype.formula: 117 Pseudo Kleinian Mod2, active scene branches only
high_low_precision_prototype.cpu_oracle: Actual native FormulaCode compiled in double precision, FPT bailout wrapper
high_low_precision_prototype.math_mode: Safe math, no implicit contraction, explicit FMA residuals
scope_limitations: Diagnostic kernel, not a selectable release renderer or voxel-export backend.
Scene-specific formula branches and parameters, not general Mandel formula support.
Identical-ray numerical comparison, not complete native beauty/appearance parity.
Timings are diagnostic dispatches, not a warmed speed benchmark; float32 fails most rays.
Generated GPL formula-derived sources and raw artifacts are ignored and not packaged.

reusable_arithmetic.scope: Experimental finite-range arithmetic only, not IEEE binary64 or general Mandel renderer support

offline_reference_command.support_policy: Exact validated scene and native formula SHA-256 only; fail before output/compilation for other inputs
offline_reference_command.source_parameters: Original parsed float64; no FptRenderConfig float32 conversion
offline_reference_command.formula_import: Native active branches imported at runtime; no bundled Mandel formula bodies
offline_reference_command.output: White camera-headlight PNG, depth, raw samples, original double rays, source fingerprints and timing report

nearby_camera_precision_gate.next: Keep the explicit scene-pinned offline reference. Expand supported formula configurations only behind independent CPU gates, or measure a faster precision implementation. Preserve the fast default; no production or CVOX support claim.

limitations: Coarse alignment is visual review, not exact depth/normal correspondence.
Native sampling and normal estimation differ from the stored FPT 32-SPP images.
A successful process/file check in backend-controls.json is not visual validation: native OpenCL scene 48 completed but its image is uniform RGB 1.

Intermediate shadow-control scripts emitted warnings for unused light IDs and a misspelled random-light flag. The final tracked helper corrected these; final captures have no unknown-override warnings.
Authored appearance findings and full-corpus support claims have not improved merely because two geometry labels were corrected.
